key_insight: An equivariant graph neural network can predict frequency-dependent complex dynamic polarizability tensors of organic molecules directly from molecular structure and spectra, capturing both dispersive and absorptive optical behavior.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster screening of photoactive organic molecules for optoelectronic device design, reducing reliance on expensive TD-DFT calculations.
method: Uses an equivariant GNN to preserve 3D molecular symmetries and tensor structure.
Learns complex-valued, frequency-dependent dynamic polarizability from 3D geometry and UV-vis spectra.
Integrates predictions into downstream optical simulations for device-level performance assessment.
evidence_signal: Across QM9 and Harvard organic photovoltaic datasets, the model reproduced key tensor features and achieved strong agreement in device simulations, with charge carrier generation rates matching TD-DFT-based results at R² = 0.94.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the availability and quality of 3D conformations and spectral inputs, and accuracy should be checked carefully when extrapolating to chemistries outside the training distribution.
paper_title: Accelerating dynamic polarizability calculations of organic molecules using equivariant graph neural networks
